title: KV cache compaction stalls causing TTL reordering and intermittent poisoning - follow-up
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a capacity ramp on 2026-02-17 we observed repeated increases in memory utilization and a small number of corrupt cache entries that led to stuttering tail latency for a subset of hosted inference requests. Investigation shows a compaction path stall in the slab allocator that reordered TTL tombstones relative to active inserts, enabling short-lived stale reads (a form of cache poisoning) and triggering downstream eviction churn. This ticket tracks the postmortem follow-ups: short-term mitigations, telemetry+alerts, correctness fixes, and verification for rollout to Dedicated/Private clusters.
incident_summary: Timeline: 2026-02-17 03:20 UTC - first alert: higher 99th tail latency on model-serving pool. 03:27 - automated eviction backpressure kicked in; 03:45 - Redis fallbacks increased. 04:10 - mitigation: throttled compaction via temporary config and drained a single faulty shard. Root cause analysis identified a race between asynchronous compaction and concurrent insert/delete that left tombstones out-of-order in slab segments. This allowed stale prefix keys to be returned during prefix scans for ~20s bursts. Impact: ~0.3% of requests seeing degraded outputs, elevated cost due to extra fallbacks, and two customer tickets (triaged as medium).
root_cause: A compaction codepath used a non-atomic two-step segment rewrite where tombstone write ordering relied on scheduling guarantees that no longer held after a scheduler change in runtime-1.26. In high insertion rate scenarios the compaction writer could preempt and resume with a different base sequence, producing segment slices that had older tombstones placed after newer live entries. The slab index lookup used segment-local offsets and did not validate global sequence monotonicity, allowing stale entries to win lookups during prefix scans.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Disable background compaction on affected runtime pools (feature-flag rollback). 2) Apply emergency validator that checks per-segment sequence monotonicity on warmup and fails open to trigger safe eviction. 3) Add a temporary prefix-scan guard: if a key's sequence < live_seq_cache for that namespace, treat as a miss. These mitigations reduce customer impact while long-term fixes land.
long_term_fixes: Rewrite compaction writer to use atomic swap of rebuilt segment (single syscall) and ensure sequence numbers are normalized before publishing (owner: Luca M., estimate: 5).
Add per-segment checksums and monotonic sequence invariants in the slab header; surface mismatch as metric (owner: Priya Kapoor, estimate: 3).
Refactor prefix-scan to consult global sequence cache (copy-on-read) to prevent stale wins; include unit+fuzz tests for concurrent compaction scenarios (owner: Diego Alvarez, estimate: 8).
Backfill a repair pass that scans segments for tombstone order anomalies and rewrites when detected; run as offline job for clusters with confirmed anomalies (owner: SRE-runbook, estimate: 5).
action_items: ENG-703214-A1: Feature-flag compaction OFF for production pools until atomic rewrite lands (owner: Luca Martinez, due: 2026-03-01, status: done).
ENG-703214-A2: Implement sequence-monotonicity validator and expose metric 'kvcache.segment.sequence_violation' (owner: Priya Kapoor, due: 2026-03-10, status: in progress).
ENG-703214-A3: Add unit+fuzz tests targeting compaction+insert/delete interleaving; CI gate before runtime-1.28 (owner: Diego Alvarez, due: 2026-03-15, status: in progress).
ENG-703214-A4: Create a repair/rewriter job and schedule for low-traffic windows; run on 2 affected clusters as pilot (owner: SRE, due: 2026-03-22, status: planned).
ENG-703214-A5: Postmortem doc and customer communication draft for affected accounts + internal blameless summary (owner: Maya Chen, due: 2026-03-05, status: done).
ENG-703214-A6: Dashboard and alert: add 'kvcache.segment.sequence_violation > 0' alert with runbook (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-08, status: in progress).
verification_plan: Canary: deploy atomic compaction to 1 host per region behind canary flag; run synthetic prefix-scan load generator for 48h and assert 99.99th latency stable.
Regression tests: add three deterministic interleavings to CI that previously reproduced the bug; require green before rollout.
Metrics: monitor 'kvcache.segment.sequence_violation', 'kvcache.eviction.churn_rate', and 99th tail latency for 24h post-rollout.
Post-deploy scan: run repair job and verify rewrite count == number of detected anomalies; zero anomalies after two consecutive scans.
risk_assessment: Risks: rollback could increase memory pressure briefly if compaction stays disabled too long; the repair job may cause higher IO on clusters during rewrite windows. Mitigations: schedule repair during off-peak, throttle rewrite IO, keep compaction disabled only until atomic publishing is verified.
notes: Customer tickets ID: C-11821 and C-11827 — both received grace credits; CS updated customers on 2026-02-19.
Root cause surfaced after adding a minimal sequence invariant check during ad-hoc debugging; earlier alerts missed the pattern because segment-slab metrics were aggregated at too-large buckets.
SRE performed a manual shard drain for the most affected host which temporarily restored tail latency but did not eliminate the underlying ordering issue.
review_feedback: PM: prioritize repair job for Dedicated customers with strict SLAs (Alex Nguyen).
Security: no customer data exfiltration pathway found; recommended code review for segment header changes (Jordan Lee).
Design: consider exposing 'sequence_repair' as an opt-in admin action in Console for private installs (Rina Patel).
